who: Howard Lee Scamehorn, historian of business and Colorado industry at the University of Colorado Boulder, PhD in history from Illinois.

evidence.says: The authority joins the names H. Lee Scamehorn, Howard Lee Scamehorn and Lee Scamehorn; its citation for High Altitude Energy (2002) identifies him as professor emeritus of history at the University of Colorado Boulder.

The indexed professional biography identifies Howard Lee Scamehorn with Colorado's Boulder history department, a history PhD from Illinois, and successive Colorado appointments beginning in 1956, including professor from 1966.

notes: Full-name variants, doctorate institution and Boulder career agree. The external biography does not separately date the PhD.

who: George Clarke Sellery, history professor and dean at Wisconsin, PhD Chicago 1901.

evidence.says: The authority equates George C. Sellery with George Clarke Sellery and associates him with E. A. Birge and the University of Wisconsin.

The indexed faculty memorial, document 1534 of March 5, 1962, records his Chicago PhD in 1901, appointment to Wisconsin history that year, professorship from 1909, and deanship from 1919 until retirement in 1942.

notes: Exact doctorate institution and year; Wisconsin service covers both students' dissertation years. Memorial evidence was available through the indexed extract.

who: Buchanan Sharp, historian of Tudor and Stuart England at UC Santa Cruz, PhD Berkeley 1971.

evidence.says: The authority's citation for Law and Authority in Early Modern England identifies Buchanan Sharp as a history professor at UC Santa Cruz.
UC Santa Cruz records his Berkeley PhD in 1971, research on Tudor/Stuart England, arrival at Santa Cruz in 1970, and forty years of university service.
The approval page for J. Brien O'Connell's English Purchasing Power dissertation lists Professor Buchanan Sharp on the committee at UC Santa Cruz; the dissertation is dated December 2012.

notes: Name, department, field and doctorate match. The repository dates the listed O'Connell dissertation December 2012, while the AHA entry gives 2013.

who: Jason Stacy, historian of the United States at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, PhD Loyola Chicago 2006.

evidence.says: The authority's Containing Multitudes citation identifies Jason Stacy as a Loyola Chicago history PhD and assistant professor of U.S. history at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville.
Loyola identifies Jason Stacy as a 2006 American history doctorate graduate and professor of history at SIU Edwardsville.
SIUE identifies Mark Neels as a 2015 graduate of the SIUE/SIUC cooperative doctorate and names SIUE's Jason Stacy and SIUC's Kay Carr as co-chairs of Lincoln's Conservatives.

notes: The joint doctoral program explains the Carbondale student record despite Stacy's Edwardsville appointment. SIUE dates Neels's graduation 2015 rather than AHA's 2014. The matching candidate is Jason Stacy, not the differently named J. G. or J. W. candidates.

who: Ivan D. Steen, public and oral historian at the University at Albany, PhD New York University.

evidence.says: The authority identifies the author of Urbanizing America as Ivan D. Steen and cites a publisher biography identifying him as associate professor of history emeritus at the University at Albany, SUNY.
Albany's faculty page lists Ivan D. Steen as associate professor emeritus in history with a PhD from New York University.
Albany's account states that Steen began teaching history there in 1960, established its public history program in 1983, and retired in 2015.

notes: The authority and faculty page identify the same Albany historian; NYU education agrees and his service covers 2010–2011.

who: Harold Coffin Syrett, historian at CUNY and editor of The Papers of Alexander Hamilton.

evidence.says: The authority connects Harold C. Syrett and Harold Coffin Syrett. Its obituary citation identifies the Hamilton papers editor, records Columbia history service in 1941–1961, and CUNY history teaching from 1969 until retirement in 1979.
The biographical account records his Columbia history PhD in 1944 and subsequent history professorship at the CUNY Graduate Center, ending in 1979.

notes: The candidate's CUNY service includes both dissertation years, and the doctorate agrees with the AHA record.

who: Lewis Arthur Tambs, professor of Latin American history at Arizona State University, PhD UC Santa Barbara.

evidence.says: The authority links Lewis A. Tambs, Lewis Arthur Tambs and Lewis Tambs and identifies him as an associate professor of history at Arizona State University.
The ASU faculty catalogue lists Lewis A. Tambs with an appointment year of 1969, as professor of history, with MA and PhD degrees from UC Santa Barbara.
ASU's memorial identifies Lewis Arthur Tambs as a Santa Barbara graduate in Latin American history, subsequently professor and director of Latin American Studies at ASU, retiring in 2002.

notes: Full-name variants, doctoral institution and ASU career agree; the appointment predates both students. These sources do not separately confirm the PhD year.

who: Eren Tasar, historian of Soviet Central Asia and Islam at UNC Chapel Hill, PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: The authority's Soviet and Muslim citation links Eren Tasar with Eren Murat Tasar and identifies him as assistant professor of history at UNC Chapel Hill.

Harvard's 2024 event biography identifies Tasar as associate professor and director of graduate studies in UNC history, author of Soviet and Muslim, and recipient of a Harvard PhD in Soviet history in 2010.
Tasar's own site identifies him as director of graduate studies in UNC's history department and describes his UNC teaching.

notes: Name, book, department, field and doctoral institution agree. Harvard dates the doctorate 2010, while the AHA dissertation entry gives 2011; this year discrepancy does not indicate a different person.
